bib.title: SkillsBench: Benchmarking How Well Agent Skills Work Across Diverse Tasks

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "SkillsBench: Benchmarking How Well Agent Skills Work Across Diverse Tasks", Xiangyi Li, Yimin Liu, Wenbo Chen, Bingran You, et al. (corresponding author Li, BenchFlow; last author Dawn Song). Preprint: the stamp reads "arXiv:2602.12670v4 [cs.AI] 14 Jun 2026", and no conference or journal is stated. 2026.

COVERAGE: 130,206 of 130,206 chars, 42 of 42 pages (the total includes my page markers). No range gaps; range boundaries checked. References were read for origins. Table 19 and the Figs 11-13 task labels were only scanned. Figures were not viewed; captions come from `figures.py`.

CLAIMS
- claim: Curated Skills raise the mean pass rate across all configurations.
  number: 33.9% to 50.5%; +16.6 pp; g = 25.5%
  setup: 87 tasks, 8 domains, 18 model-harness configs, 2 conditions, 3 trials per cell = 9,396 trials; temperature 0; deterministic verifier. g is macro-averaged per config.
  quote: "Curated Skills raise the average pass rate from 33.9% to 50.5% (+16.6 percentage points; 25.5% normalized gain), with configuration-level gains ranging from +4.1 to +25.7 pp."
  where: p1; Table 2 p6
- claim: Lift varies by stack, and the best absolute systems are not the biggest gainers.
  number: best 67.3%; largest lift +25.7 pp; smallest +4.1 pp
  setup: same frame; best = OpenHands + GPT-5.5; largest = OpenHands + GLM 5.1 (32.7 to 58.4); smallest = OpenHands + Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite (16.0 to 20.1).
  quote: "The highest with-Skills pass rates are OpenHands + GPT-5.5 (67.3%), Codex + GPT-5.5 (66.5%), and Claude Code + Opus 4.7 (61.2%). The largest lifts instead come from OpenHands + GLM 5.1 (+25.7 pp; 38.1% normalized gain)"
  where: p5
- claim: Self-generated Skills score below no Skills at all on every config tested.
  number: -8.1, -11.3, -11.5 pp; curated +18.2 to +24.8 pp
  setup: 3 dedicated-harness configs only, as a diagnostic outside the main aggregate; creator session uses Anthropic's skill-creator, then a clean solver session. Rows (no/self/curated): CC Opus 4.7 43.0/34.9/61.2; Codex GPT-5.5 46.8/35.5/66.5; Gemini CLI 3.1 Pro 36.0/24.5/60.8.
  quote: "Self-generated Skills land below the no-Skills baseline on all three configurations ( −8.1 pp on Claude Code + Opus 4.7, −11.3 pp on Codex + GPT-5.5, −11.5 pp on Gemini CLI + Gemini 3.1 Pro)"
  where: p7; Table 6 p22
- claim: Audited self-generated packs mostly went unread, and the clearest win was an answer key written inside the graded sandbox.
  number: 10 of 12 audited trajectories; 1.0 vs 0.0 on fix-visual-stability
  setup: 12 solver trajectories across 10 (task, config) pairs, selected for extreme gaps. The "10 of 12" applies to the pre-baked Codex and Gemini CLI family.
  quote: "10 of 12 audited trajectories never list, read, or mention the generated skills"; "(self-generated 1.0 vs. curated 0.0 on Claude Code), works because the creator wrote the pack inside the graded sandbox"
  where: p23
- claim: The same model gains differently under different harnesses.
  number: Gemini 3.1 Pro 60.8 vs 52.8; Opus 4.7 61.2 vs 53.1; GPT-5.5 67.3 vs 66.5
  setup: with-Skills pass rates; 3 model families run on two harnesses each.
  quote: "GPT-5.5 reaches 67.3% with Skills in OpenHands and 66.5% in Codex; Gemini 3.1 Pro reaches 60.8% in Gemini CLI but 52.8% in OpenHands; Claude Opus 4.7 reaches 61.2% in Claude Code and 53.1% in OpenHands."
  where: p6
- claim: Domain lift ranges widely, largest in specialised science and smallest in maths and software.
  number: +28.8 pp to +9.7 pp
  setup: N = 5 to 16 tasks per domain, macro-averaged across 18 configs. Authors call the N<8 domains (Cybersecurity, Media) descriptive only (p38).
  quote: "Natural Science (+28.8 pp), Media & Content Production (+24.1 pp), and Cybersecurity (+18.9 pp) benefit most; Software Engineering (+11.6 pp) and Mathematics & OR (+9.7 pp) benefit least."
  where: p7
- claim: Skills lower the aggregate score on some tasks.
  number: 13 of 87 tasks; worst -7.4 pp
  setup: per-task delta across configs; causes come from a paired trajectory audit (heavy pipeline, displaced native strategy, solver the agent cannot debug).
  quote: "13 of 87 tasks show negative Skills deltas; the largest drops occur on exam-block-sequencing (−7.4 pp), suricata-custom-exfil (−7.4 pp)"
  where: p7; p28
- claim: Fewer, shorter Skills gain more than many or exhaustive ones.
  number: 1 Skill +18.0, 2-3 +19.0, 4 or more +10.1; compact +19.0, standard +21.5, detailed +14.5, comprehensive +0.7
  setup: observational split across tasks, not randomised. N = 23/43/21 by count; N = 22/22/38/5 by length. Baselines differ by bucket (standard 19.8%, compact 37.6%).
  quote: "tasks paired with one Skill gain +18.0 pp, 2–3 Skills gain +19.0 pp, and ≥4 Skills give only +10.1 pp"; "compact and standard-length Skills (+19.0 and +21.5 pp) outperform detailed (+14.5 pp) and comprehensive documentation (+0.7 pp)"
  where: p7-8; Tables 8-9 p28
- claim: Authors say discovery is usually not the bottleneck, though invocation varies about twofold.
  number: invocation 46.4% to 99.2%
  setup: curated-Skills trials; only task-bundled Skills counted, usually out of 261 trials. Resolution given invocation is conditional, not causal.
  quote: "Codex GPT-5.5 99.2% 259/261 66.5% 66.2%"; "OpenHands Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite 46.4% 121/261 20.1% 29.8%"; "High Skill Invocation Rate does not guarantee high resolution"
  where: Table 14 p33; p7
- claim: A smaller model with Skills can beat some larger models without them.
  number: 34.9% vs 32.7% and 29.7%
  setup: MiniMax M2.7 with Skills against two chosen no-Skills baselines. Table 2 shows other no-Skills baselines above it, such as GPT-5.5 at 51.5.
  quote: "MiniMax M2.7 with Skills (34.9%) exceeds stronger no-Skills baselines such as OpenHands + GLM 5.1 (32.7%) and OpenHands + MiniMax M3 (29.7%)"
  where: p8
- claim: "Pass rate" includes partial credit, so strict solves are slightly lower.
  number: solved 31.3% to 47.7%, against 33.9% to 50.5%
  setup: 4,698 trials per condition. Attempted = verifier-scored reward 0. Runtime errors count as 0.
  quote: "No Skills 4,698 31.3% 5.4% 62.7% 0.6%"; "Curated Skills 4,698 47.7% 4.7% 46.5% 1.0%"
  where: Table 16 p34
- claim: Cost per trial does not track capability, and Skills move tokens in either direction.
  number: $1.67 vs $14.02; 1.82M to 4.02M tokens; 1.77M to 1.09M tokens
  setup: mean per trial, computed through LiteLLM. Cost exists for only 10 of 18 configs; Claude Code counts are approximate.
  quote: "OpenHands + GPT-5.5 attains the highest with-Skills pass rate (67.3%) at $1.67 per trial—about eight times cheaper than OpenHands + Claude Opus 4.8 (54.1% at $14.02)"; "OpenHands + Gemini 3.1 Pro 1.82M→ 4.02M"; "OpenHands + Claude Opus 4.7 1.77M→ 1.09M"
  where: p35
- claim: Skills add little or no agent time at fleet level.
  number: +16.6 pp; 10.0 to 6.5 minutes for one config
  setup: mean agent wall-clock per task, agent runtime only.
  quote: "Curated Skills lift the fleet mean by +16.6 pp at broadly unchanged agent time; the slower half of the fleet runs faster with Skills (e.g., OpenHands + Claude Opus 4.7: 10.0→ 6.5 minutes per task)."
  where: p35
- claim: A narrow set of tasks moves enormously.
  number: top-10 mean +67.0 pp; llm-prefix-cache-replay 1.9% to 94.4%
  setup: per-task average across configs. Authors' audit credits scripts with calibrated defaults, canonical data sources, verifier-facing format constraints, invariants and specific `description:` frontmatter (p8, p28-29).
  quote: "llm-prefix-cache-replay reaches 94.4% from a 1.9% no-Skills pass rate"
  where: p7; Table 13 p33
- claim: Benchmark Skills are much better than typical ecosystem Skills, which authors call an optimistic scenario.
  number: 10.1/12 vs 6.2/12
  setup: authors' own 4-part rubric; ecosystem count 2,014,000 Skills, cloned sample 767,430. Mean is 6.2 (SD 2.8).
  quote: "Real-world Skill usage involves lower-quality Skills (ecosystem mean: 6.2/12 vs. benchmark mean: 10.1/12) and imperfect Skill-task matching."
  where: p15
- claim: Tasks were heavily filtered, and Skills may not contain instance answers.
  number: 87 of 400 submissions; 142 contributors; 22%
  setup: automated gates (structure, oracle at 100%, GPTZero plus human provenance, leakage audit) followed by maintainer review.
  quote: "Of 400 candidate submissions from 142 contributors, 87 tasks passed all review stages and are included in the current benchmark inventory (22% acceptance rate)."
  where: p17; p4
- claim: Runtime failures are rare and mostly command timeouts.
  number: 78 of 9,396 (0.8%); 72 command timeouts
  setup: trials with no scored result, counted as reward 0.
  quote: "Runtime errors in the latest 18-configuration aggregate (trials with no scored result; 78 of 9,396 = 0.8%)"; "Command timeout 72"
  where: Table 17 p35

LIMITS
Conceded by the authors:
- Results are for terminal-based, containerized tasks and "may not transfer directly to GUI agents, multi-agent coordination, or very long-horizon workflows" (p8).
- Gains "could partly reflect “more context” rather than procedural structure"; no length-matched control was run (p8).
- The self-generated deficit "mixes content quality with skill-discovery and creator/solver interference effects" (p8).
- They "cannot eliminate all nondeterminism or memorization effects" (p8).
- Claude models were "trained with awareness of the Agent Skills specification" (p21, p42).
- Normalized gain "can overstate small absolute gains near the ceiling" (p42).
- Self-generated deviations: Claude Code used effort `max` against `high` at baseline (p22), and scored slots were 258, 258 and 253 of 261 (p22). The 3d-scan-calc verifier was patched ten days after those runs (p23).

Not conceded, my reading of the text:
- Selection on the outcome. "tasks with no measurable separation between conditions are rejected as low-signal" (p4), and "tasks solvable without any procedural guidance are rejected" (p18). The headline lift is therefore measured on tasks screened for showing Skill benefit. It is not an estimate for arbitrary tasks. The authors' optimism caveat names Skill quality and matching, not this.
- Statistics are thin. CIs are unpaired Wald intervals treating 261 trials as independent (p29), though trials are nested in 87 tasks; there is no significance test, and normalized gain has no interval.
- My arithmetic: half-width is about ±6 pp at p near 0.5, so Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite's +4.1 and Gemini 3.5 Flash's +7.1 have overlapping intervals (overlap is not a paired test).
- My arithmetic: each task-condition has 54 trials if binary, so -7.4 pp is about 4 trials and -5.6 pp about 3. The negative-delta "failure modes" are close to noise size.
- My arithmetic: Table 12's 9.8% runtime errors for OpenHands + Sonnet 4.6 is about 51 of the 78 errors, all scored 0, which depresses that config's figures.
- Harness comparison is thin. 15 of 18 configs use OpenHands, and only 3 families span two harnesses.
- Metrics not reported: pass@k, pass^k, or per-task variance over trials. Three trials at temperature 0 gives only a mean. Cost per success is not reported either.

Dated: model lineup is as of June 2026; harness Skill integration "can change over time" (p8).

Conflict of interest: the lead affiliation, BenchFlow, builds the harness the benchmark runs on (p1, p5). Vendors provided model access and API support (p9).

BUILDS ON
- Merrill et al., 2026 (Terminal-Bench): task-macro scoring
- Hake, 1998: normalized gain
- Anthropic, 2025a: Agent Skills format and progressive disclosure
- Harbor Framework Team, 2026: task format that `task.md` extends
- BenchFlow team, 2026: harness
- Liu et al., 2023: named as closest paired-evaluation precedent (see PROBLEMS)
- Wang et al., 2023b and Brown, 2025: cited against LLM-as-judge verification
- Sutton et al., 1999 and Sumers et al., 2024: Skills as modular procedural artifacts
- Mattson et al., 2020; Chiang et al., 2024; Srivastava et al., 2023: benchmarking practice

CODE
Normalized gain, p5: `g= (pass skill −pass vanilla)/(1−pass vanilla),(1)`

Canonical verifier, `test.sh`, p16:
```
pytest --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json \
/verifier/test_outputs.py -rA -v
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
echo 1 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
else
echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
fi
```

FIGURES (none viewed)
- Fig 1, p1: "Agent architecture stack and resolution rates across 18 model–harness configurations on 87 SkillsBench tasks." Baseline plus lift per stack shows the headline and its spread at a glance. Check it visually first (see PROBLEMS).
- Fig 3, p4: "Anatomy of a SKILLSBENCH task." Shows given vs withheld material and the three paired arms with their lift formulas. Best fit for explaining paired evaluation.
- Fig 5, p6: "Task-specific Skill Invocation Rate alongside resolution rates." Shows access and benefit diverging.
- Fig 10, p23: "Self-generated Skills underperform not only curated Skills but the no-Skills baseline". Three-way result in one small chart.
- Fig 13, p27: "Skills uplift per task (with Skills − without Skills)." Shows per-task heterogeneity and where Skills hurt.
- Fig 15, p36: "Resolution rate vs. mean agent wall-clock per task (minutes, log scale)". Time against capability, before and after.
- Figs 2 (p3), 4 (p4), 11-12 (p25-26) and 14 (p30) are also available. Figs 6-9 (p13-15) cover ecosystem statistics.

PROBLEMS
- No instructions addressed to a reader or reviewer were found. The creator prompt on p22 ("Do not solve the task directly") is quoted experimental material, and I treated it as data.
- Extraction: quotes above have line breaks collapsed, and italic spacing is sometimes lost. Equations are partly garbled (pp29, 42). Table values are read from flattened rows.
- Page 1 text holds a second chart's labels (Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.6, GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, "Self-Generated") that the Fig 1 caption does not describe. This may be a hidden layer from an earlier version, so check the rendered image before reuse.
- Internal inconsistencies:
  - Verifier output is described as pass/fail (p5, p16), but as a fraction in [0,1] (p4, p42) with partial outcomes (p34).
  - "Reasoning effort: Highest available" (p24) conflicts with the Claude Code baseline at `high` (p22).
  - An "8K token limit" sliding window (p24) sits oddly beside mean totals over 1M tokens per trial (p34) and native harness runs, and may be stale.
  - Top-quartile selection of Skills (p15) sits oddly beside Skills authored independently by contributors (p3). "3–6 Skills" per task (p18) conflicts with 23 single-Skill tasks (p28).
  - Table 14 shows MiniMax M3 at 177/258, while Table 5 shows 261/261.
  - `gh-repo-analytics` (p32) is not in the 87-task list in Table 19.
  - Appendix F cites "Finding 5" for what is Finding 6.
  - §3 promises per-gate rejection counts in Appendix M; I found none.
  - Table 5 is said to list harness versions (p42), but does not; Table 7's "Harness Version" column gives harness names only.
- Possible mis-citation: the paired precedent on "enterprise API workflows" with "paired bootstrap CIs" is cited as [Liu et al., 2023] (p9), and the only matching reference entry is AgentBench (p11). I did not check AgentBench, so verify before repeating this lineage.
